title: Lesson 82 - Who's Responsible for the Damage?

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: We are reviewing responsibility, not assuming it. Can we hear from Leo on what was inspected, packed and recorded before the courier collected the unit?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: The unit passed a basic power and screen check at 7:18 Monday. We had the mounting bracket inspected visually, and the checklist records no visible bend.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Was the item photographed from every side before it was packed?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: No. The 7:24 image shows the screen, front of the stand and left side. The lower-right bracket area is partly hidden by the base.

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: Who packed it, and was the protective insert checked?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: A warehouse technician packed it at 7:31. The box was sealed and scanned at 7:42, but the checklist confirms only that the standard insert was present, not its exact position.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Then the dispatch record supports a basic inspection and sealed box, but it does not show the bracket clearly or prove the insert was aligned.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: That is correct. We had the package collected by the courier at 8:05. Their handoff scan reports no exception, but it has no photograph.

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: The delivery image at 10:18 shows a crease near the lower-right corner. Aisha’s receipt also records visible damage before unpacking.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I had it delivered by the courier ClearView selected. I did not arrange a separate carrier or move the sealed box to another address.

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: What evidence is responsibility currently based on? We have a limited dispatch image, a clean handoff scan without a photo, a damaged-box delivery record and customer images taken fourteen minutes later.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Taken together, those records suggest the bracket could have been bent before packing or during transit. They do not show the exact moment of damage.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Could it have been damaged after delivery but before I photographed it?

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: That possibility cannot be excluded by time alone, but the sealed-box note, short interval and your decision not to power it on all remain relevant. Possibility is not evidence that you caused it.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: The unit needs to be assessed by a technician. The bracket, protective insert and impact marks may show whether the force came through the damaged corner.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Will that assessment decide who is responsible?

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: It may narrow the likely stage, but one inspection may not identify a person or prove a single cause. Responsibility hasn’t been determined yet.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I also need to correct one phrase in the warehouse note. “Bracket inspected” could sound more complete than the actual visual check shown in the photo.

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: Are we ready to determine responsibility? No. We are ready to authorize technical assessment, preserve the charge pause and compare the report with every earlier record.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Is that an accurate record: dispatch condition is only partly documented, transit condition has a gap and customer-caused damage has not been established?
